title: Kept in Repair

cast.name: Ciro Avellan
cast.portrait: Mid twenties in 1991; light-brown skin, short straight black hair, dark-brown eyes, lean build and a narrow, watchful face; plain olive-gray flight suit with no patches.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Ciro comes south from training with good reports and a habit of mending his own mistakes before anyone finds them. He wants to be trusted with the field's few aircraft and to deserve it. He fears that the first thing people learn about him will be something he broke, and that they will never learn anything else.

cast.name: Lucia Ferro
cast.portrait: Late twenties in 1991; olive skin, long dark-brown hair tied in a low knot, hazel eyes, a quick wide smile and a medium, athletic build; plain sand-colored flight suit.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Lucia has flown from the southern field for three years and knows half the shore road by name. She promises easily and keeps most of what she promises, which makes the rest harder to admit. She wants to be the person everyone can count on, and fears the moment she must say no to someone's face.

cast.name: Ines Carvalho
cast.portrait: Early thirties in 1991; medium-brown skin, short black curly hair, dark-brown eyes behind reading glasses pushed up on her head, sturdy build; plain dark-green maintenance coveralls.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Ines runs the field's maintenance with too few parts and a green cloth-bound ledger of her own, in which she writes what did not work and why. She wants the next crew to inherit causes rather than rumors. She fears the ledger becoming either a list of blame or a secret only she can read.

cast.name: Hector Mendaro
cast.portrait: Early thirties in 1991; fair, sun-weathered skin with deep squint lines, thinning sandy-brown hair, blue-gray eyes, a broad heavy build; plain white short-sleeved shirt and an unmarked headset.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Hector controls the field's traffic and keeps its peace with the coast station, the fishing cooperative and the civil airport across the runway, mostly by telephone and coffee. He wants every neighbor to keep saying yes. He fears that one honest disagreement written on paper could undo years of quiet arrangements.

1.title: The hangar on its rail
1.subject: A small coastal hangar in early morning light, its big sliding doors half open on their floor rails. Inside, an older conventional aircraft sits partly under canvas; along one wall a long workbench holds a green cloth-bound ledger, and a wooden crate rests on a low trailer with a plain cardboard tag tied to its handle. Two people in plain flight suits and one in coveralls talk beside the bench, faces partly turned away.

2.title: The tower window
2.subject: A small control tower cab at dusk overlooking a wet runway edge and a gray sea. A controller seen from behind wears an unmarked headset; an old radio set with a second handset sits beside a small softly glowing screen with no readable marks. A plain brown cardboard tag hangs on a nail beside the window, and a second person waits in the doorway holding two mugs.

3.title: The bench under the lamp
3.subject: A maintenance bench under a single hanging lamp at night: an opened conventional aircraft component, a fine file, a few small hand tools spilling from a dented biscuit tin, and a green ledger lying open on blank pages. In the background a folded maintenance stand leans against the wall with a strip of plain red cloth tied around one leg. Two pairs of working hands, no faces.

4.title: The gate on the shore road
4.subject: An airfield chain-link gate and small guard hut on a coastal road under overcast light, with the sea and a stony cove below. A handful of people in ordinary dark coats gather at the gate, some carrying bags or folded blankets, one pulling a small boat trailer, while two crew members in plain jackets talk with them. A parked utility van and wheeling gulls; no signs, flags or insignia.

5.title: The crew room table
5.subject: A plain crew room at evening: a long wooden table with four mismatched chairs, a stack of green cloth-bound ledgers, a closed folder and an open dented biscuit tin. Through the window, a darkened apron with one conventional aircraft standing under a single work light. Warm lamplight inside, cool blue dusk outside, and nobody's face in view.

6.title: The tenth volume
6.subject: Late warm light through open hangar doors onto a workbench. A young technician writes in an open green ledger while four older people stand and sit close around her, one leaning in to point at the page, one smiling. A worn door wheel and a cardboard tag lie on the bench beside the ledger. Relaxed, attentive and unceremonious; faces partly turned away.

7.title: The locked cabinet
7.subject: A tidy crew room office in flat afternoon light. A neat printed binder lies squarely on a clean desk; behind it a glass-fronted cabinet holds a row of green cloth-bound ledgers behind a small closed lock. Through a doorway two people talk quietly in the next room, while two others work apart at a far bench. Orderly, careful distance and no confrontation.

8.title: Different doors
8.subject: A changing room at the end of a shift: four metal lockers, one standing open and empty with its inner door wiped to a gray smear; a dented biscuit tin left alone on a bench; a travel bag by the wall. Through two separate doorways, figures walk away in different directions into gray daylight. Quiet and unresolved, with no injury, funeral or mourning.

loading_subject: A small airfield on a southern coast at early morning: one runway running along the shore, two modest hangars with sliding doors, a squat control tower, and the low terminal of a civil airport across the field. Fishing boats rest in a stony cove below the perimeter road. Low sun, salt haze and still air.
